semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {لاَ تُقَدِّمُواْ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the qāf and the dāl doubled with kasra, and there are two views about it. The first: that it is transitive and its object is omitted, either for brevity, as in their saying "he gives and withholds", {وَكُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 187], or by way of abbreviation because it is indicated, that is: "do not put forward what is not fitting." The second: that it is intransitive, like «وَجَّه» and «تَوَجَّه», supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk «لا تَقَدَّمُوا» with fatḥa in the three letters; the original is «لا تَتَقَدَّمُوْا», one of the two tāʾs being dropped. Some Meccans read «لا تَّقَدَّمُوْا» likewise, / except with the tāʾ doubled, like the tāʾs of al-Bazzī. That which is reached by the preposition in these two readings is also omitted, that is: "do not advance to any matter." «لا تُقْدِموا» was also read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the dāl, from «أَقْدَمَ», that is: "do not venture upon anything."

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {أَن تَحْبَطَ}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The matter is one of tanāzuʿ (competing operators), because each of His sayings «لا تَرْفَعوا» and {لاَ تَجْهَرُواْ لَهُ} demands it in meaning; so it is governed by the second according to the Basrans' preference, and by the first according to the Kufans. The first is sounder because of the omission from the first, that is: «لأَنْ تحبطَ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra)", and there is no need for that. {وَأَنتُمْ لاَ تَشْعُرُونَ} is a ḥāl.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أولئك}: «أولئك» may be a mubtadaʾ with «الذين» as its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of «إنَّ», and «لهم مغفرةٌ» another sentence: either resumptive, which is the apparent sense, or a ḥāl clause. It is also possible that «الذين امتحنَ» is an adjective of «أولئك», or a badal from it, or an explicative apposition, with «لهم مغفرةٌ» a predicative sentence. It is also possible that «لهم» alone is the khabar and «مغفرةٌ» is its agent.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {مِن وَرَآءِ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range. In al-Zamakhsharī's discussion there is something that denies that «مِنْ» can mean both the beginning and the end of the range. He said: "because one and the same thing cannot be both the starting point and the end point of the action." Some people affirmed this and claimed that it indicates the beginning and end of the action in a single direction, as in «أَخَذْتُ الدرهمَ من الكيس» ("I took the dirham from the purse"). The majority read «الحُجُرات» with two ḍammas. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with fatḥa. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with sukūn. These are three dialectal forms, verified earlier in al-Baqara at His saying {فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ} [al-Baqara: 17]. «الحُجْرَةُ» is a «فُعْلَة» in the sense of «مَفْعولة», like «غُرْفة» in the sense of «مَغْروفة».

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُواْ}: the like of it has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī made it an agent of an implied verb, that is: "had their patience been established", and made the ism of «كان» a pronoun returning to this agent. It has already been said that Sībawayh's school is that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and then the ism of «كان» is a pronoun returning to their patience, understood from the verb.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {أَن تُصِيببُواْ}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, like His saying {أَن تَحْبَطَ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 2].

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ}: it may be a ḥāl, either from the genitive pronoun in «فيكم», or from the latent nominative pronoun in «فيكم», since [the other] leads to a discord in the composition. What he said is not apparent; rather, the resumptive is also clear. He used the imperfect after «لو» to indicate that it was in their wish that his action continue according to what they fabricate.
His saying: {ولكن الله}: the istidrāk (rectification) here is by meaning, not by wording, because the one to whom faith was made beloved differs in description from the one mentioned earlier.
And His saying: {أولئك هُمُ} is an iltifāt from address to the third person.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فَضْلاً}: it may be accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. There are two views about what governs it. The first: His saying {ولكن الله حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ}, and on this what lies between them, His saying {أولئك هُمُ الراشدون}, is parenthetical. The second: that it is «الراشدون». On this, how is it permissible with a different agent, since the agent of right guidance is not the agent of bounty? al-Zamakhsharī answered: "Since right guidance came to be an expression for making beloved, adorning and making disliked, all attributed to His names, right guidance became as if it were His act." He also allowed it to be accusative by an implied verb, that is: "that took place" or "that was". The Shaykh said: "This is not one of the places for implying «كان»", and he considered his first statement to be Muʿtazilism. It is not so, because he meant the verb attributed to its agent in wording; otherwise the verified position is that all acts are created by Allah the Exalted, even if al-Zamakhsharī does not agree with that. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar of emphasis for the content of the preceding sentence, because it too is bounty; but Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it a maṣdar of self-emphasis. al-Ḥūfī allowed it to be accusative as ḥāl, which is not apparent, the implied form being: "bestowing favour, granting grace", or "possessed of bounty and favour".

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {اقتتلوا}: it returns to the individuals of the two groups, as in His saying {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا} [al-Ḥajj: 19], and in «بينهما» it follows the wording. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «اقْتتلَتا», taking the wording into account. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «اقتتلا» also, except that he made the verb masculine considering the two parties, or because it is a figurative feminine.
His saying: {حتى تفياء}: the majority read it with hamza, from «فاء يَفيء», that is, he returned, like «جاء يجيْء». al-Zuhrī read it with a yāʾ with fatḥa, like the imperfect of «وَفَى»; this is in the dialect of those who shorten and say «جا، يَجي» without hamza, and then he put fatḥa on the yāʾ because it became the final letter of declension. /

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ}: the majority read the dual. Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, Ḥammād ibn Salama and Ibn Sīrīn read «إخوانِكم» in the plural on the pattern «فِعْلان». It has already been said that «الإِخوان» predominates for friendship and «الإِخْوَة» for kinship, and it may be reversed, as in this verse. From Abū ʿAmr and a group «إخْوَتِكم» with tāʾ (from above) is reported. All three readings are also reported from Abū ʿAmr.
The disagreement about «القوم» has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī made it here a plural of «قائم», saying: "like «صَوْم» and «زَوْر», plurals of «صائم» and «زائر»", but «فَعْل» is not among the patterns of the broken plural except according to al-Akhfash, as in «رَكْب» and «صَحْب».
Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «عَسَوْا» and «عَسَيْنَ», treating it as a defective verb (i.e. as a regular verb with suffixes), which is the dialect of Tamīm. The majority read it in the Ḥijāzī dialect. al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read «ولا تَلْمُزوا» with ḍamma. «اللَّمْزُ» is by speech and otherwise, and «الهَمْزُ» with the tongue only.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَنَابَزُواْ}: «التنابُزُ» is a «تفاعُل» from «النَّبْزِ», which is calling by nickname. And «النَّزْبُ» is transposed from it, given the rarity of this and the frequency of that; one says «تنابَزُوا» and «تنازَبُوا» when they call each other by a bad nickname. Its origin is from raising, as if the nickname raises its bearer so that he is seen. «اللَّقَبُ» is what indicates the lowliness of the one named, like «قُفَّة» and «بَطَّة», or his eminence, like «الصِّدِّيق», «عتيق», «الفاروق», «أسدِ الله» and «أسدِ رسوله». It has, together with the name and the kunya, rulings which I have mentioned in grammar.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِثْمٌ}: al-Zamakhsharī made its hamza a substitute for a wāw, saying: "because it «يَثِمُ» the deeds, that is, it breaks them." This is not conceded; rather that is another root. «ولا تَجَسَّسوا»: «التجسُّسُ» is following up; from it come «الجاسوس» (spy) and «الجَسَّاسَةُ». «جَواسُّ الإِنسان» and «حواسُّه» are his faculties of perception. al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn Sīrīn read it here with ḥāʾ.
His saying: {مَيْتاً}: accusative as ḥāl from «لحم» or «أخيه». The disagreement about «مَيْتا» was given earlier.
His saying: {فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ}: al-Farrāʾ said: "Its implied form is: 'then you have disliked it, so do not do it.'" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "That to which it is conjoined is omitted, its implied form being: 'That was presented to you and you disliked it', the meaning being: 'It is presented to you and you dislike it.' It is also said: 'If that is established with you, then you dislike it.'" It is also said: it is a report with the sense of a command, as in their saying "May a man who did good fear Allah; he will be rewarded for it." Abū Ḥaywa and al-Jaḥdarī read «فَكُرِّهْتُموه» with ḍamma on the kāf and the rāʾ doubled, made transitive by doubling to a second [object], unlike His first saying {وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الكفر} [verse 7], which, though doubled, takes only one object because it includes the sense of «بَغَّض» (to make hateful).

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوباً وَقَبَآئِلَ}: «الشُّعوب» is the plural of «شَعْب», which is the highest of the levels of lineage. The levels of lineage the Arabs have are six: the shaʿb, the qabīla, the ʿimāra, the baṭn, the fakhidh and the faṣīla, each entering into the one before: the faṣīla enters into the fakhidh and the fakhidh into the baṭn. Some people added after the fakhidh the ʿashīra, making seven. The shaʿb was called shaʿb because the tribes branch (tashaʿʿub) out of it, and the tribes were so called because of their facing one another (taqābul), likened to the qabāʾil of the head, which are opposing pieces. It is also said: the shuʿūb are among the non-Arabs, the qabāʾil among the Arabs, and the asbāṭ among the Children of Israel. It is also said: the shaʿb is the more distant lineage and the qabīla the nearer. And he recited:
4086 - قبائلُ مِنْ شُعوبٍ ليس فيهِمْ ... كريمٌ قد يُعَدُّ ولا نَجيبُ
(Tribes from peoples among whom there is no noble man worth counting, nor any distinguished one.)
The attribution to the shaʿb is «شَعوبيَّة» with fatḥa on the shīn; they are a people who hate the Arabs.
His saying: {لتعارفوا}: the majority read it with the tāʾ light; the original is «لتتعارفوا», one tāʾ being dropped. al-Bazzī reads it with the tāʾ doubled. That was given earlier in al-Baqara. The lām is attached to «جَعَلْناكم». al-Aʿmash read it with two tāʾs, which is the original that al-Bazzī assimilated and the majority dropped one of. Ibn ʿAbbās read «لِتَعْرِفُوا», the imperfect of «عَرَفَ». The majority read «إنَّ أكْرَمَكم» with kasra. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with fatḥa: if you make the lām the lām of command, which is remote, it becomes clear that His saying «أنَّ أَكْرَمَكم» with fatḥa is the object of knowing: He commanded them to know that. If you make it the lām of cause, it is not apparent that it be an object, because He did not make them peoples and tribes so that they know that; so the object ought to be made omitted and the lām for cause, that is: "so that you may know the truth, because the most honoured of you..."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ}: this sentence is resumptive; the Exalted informs of that. al-Zamakhsharī made it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قولوا». The discussion of «لَمَّا», what it indicates and the difference between it and «لم» has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: after His saying «لم تؤمنوا» it resembles repetition without a new benefit; I say: it is not so, for the benefit of His saying «لم تؤمنوا» is to give the lie to their claim, and «لَمَّا يَدْخُل» fixes a time limit for what they were commanded to say." Then he said: "What is in «لَمَّا» of the sense of expectation is evidence that these later believed." The Shaykh said: "I do not know in what respect what is negated by «لَمَّا» occurs afterwards." I say: because it negates «قد فَعَلَ», and «قد» is for expectation.
His saying: {لاَ يَلِتْكُمْ}: Abū ʿAmr read «لا يَأْلِتْكُمْ» with hamza, from «أَلَتَه يَأْلُتُهُ» with fatḥa in the past and kasra or ḍamma in the imperfect, and al-Sūsī replaces the hamza with alif according to his principle. The others read «يَلِتْكم», from «لاته يَليتُه» like «باعه يَبيعه», which is the Ḥijāzī dialect; the first is the dialect of Ghaṭafān and Asad. It is also said that it is from «وَلَتَه يَلِتُه» like «وَعَده يَعِدُه»; so the omitted letter on the first view is the ʿayn of the word and its pattern is «يَفِلْكم», and on the second its fāʾ and its pattern is «يَعِلْكم». One also says «ألاتَه يُليته» / like «أَباعه يُبِيعه», and «آلتَهَ يُؤْلِتُه» like «آمَنَ يُؤْمِنُ». All of these are dialectal forms with the meaning: he diminished him of his due. al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: 4087 - أَبْلِغْ سَراةَ بني سعدٍ مُغَلْغَلَةً ... جَهْدَ الرسالةِ لا أَلْتاً ولا كَذِباً
(Convey to the nobles of Banū Saʿd a message carried far, the utmost of messages, with no diminishing and no falsehood.)
And Ruʾba said:
4088 - وليلةٍ ذاتِ ندىً سَرَيْتُ ... ولم يَلِتْني عن سُراها ليتُ
(Many a night full of dew I journeyed, and nothing held me back from travelling it.)
that is: it did not prevent me or restrain me.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {أَتُعَلِّمُونَ}: this is derived by doubling from «عَلِمْتُ به» in the sense of "I was aware of it", hence it is transitive to one object by itself and to another with the bāʾ.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أَنْ أَسْلَمُواْ}: two views are permissible. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, because «يَمُنُّون» is taken to include the sense of «يَعْتَدُّون» (they count as a favour), as if it were said: "they count their Islam as a favour upon you, reproaching you with it"; hence he made the direct object explicit in His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ}, that is: "do not count your Islam as a favour upon me." Thus the Shaykh argued from this. There is room for doubt in it, for one may say: we do not concede that «إسلامَكم» is accusative as a direct object; rather it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, as it is permissible in the position of «أَنْ أَسْلَموا», which is the second view, that is: "they reproach you because they submitted"; likewise in His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ}, the conditions of the accusative are present, and the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, when annexed, may equally be genitive with a preposition or accusative.
And His saying: {أَنْ هَداكُمْ} is like «أن أَسْلَموا». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إذ هَداكم» with «إذ» in place of «أَنْ», which gives the sense of cause. The apodosis of the condition is implied, that is: "then it is He who confers favour upon you, not you upon Him or upon me."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {والله بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ}: Ibn Kathīr read it in the third person, looking to His saying «يَمُنُّون» and what follows it; the others in the second person, looking to His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ} to the end.
